subject: Post-call: Pilot readiness & ops check — dedicated hardware and streaming needs
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@cerebrolabs.com>
Cc: Cerebro Labs SRE <sre@cerebrolabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Pilot readiness & ops check — dedicated hardware and streaming needs

Hi Alyssa / SRE team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the items we agreed to validate for the dedicated pilot and next steps so we all have the same checklist: 

- Latency SLO: target 95th percentile tail <= 150ms for single-turn streaming transcripts (avg token RTT after first token).
- Throughput need: sustained 6,000 tokens/sec across the reserved pool during business hours (US PST window), burst to 10k tokens/sec for short periods.
- Concurrency: expect up to 60 concurrent real-time streams (each ~20 concurrent decoding threads on our side for multiplexed clients), with average sequence length ~120 tokens and spikes to 800 tokens for long transcripts.
- Streaming behavior: low initial latency is critical — prefer model/infra combo that minimizes first-token delay. KV cache must persist across short reconnections.
- Data plane: VPC private deployment preferred; sample logs will be shared for network shaping expectations.

Action items we captured: 
1) Red: we'll run a short hardware comparison matrix (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB vs L4/multi-L4 cluster for cost-optimized streaming) and return recommended reserved throughput (tokens/sec) and suggested pool sizing. Deliverable: recommendation doc + cost delta. Owner: Ben Carter. ETA: 2026-10-13 EOD.
2) Cerebro: share a 24-hour sample of token arrival patterns + RTP logs (you mentioned you have a day of traffic). Attachment placeholder noted. Owner: Alyssa. ETA: 2026-10-12 EOD.
3) Marcus and Hannah: define the canary plan for the pilot (routing, fallback policies to lower-cost model variant on overload). Deliverable: canary checklist. ETA: 2026-10-15.

I've attached the spreadsheet we used to map some rough throughput numbers. Ben — I left some rough fields for you to fill in. 

If that captures everything, we'll proceed on the HW comparison and reconvene after Ben's recommendation.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah — that looks right to me. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 6k tokens/sec is a conservative sustained baseline; our customers have long-tail spikes during demos — plan for an operational burst to ~10k for 3–5 minutes.
- Concurrency: 60 concurrent RT streams is our 99th percentile; median is closer to 22 streams.
- Sequence length: the 800-token spike happens ~2% of the time during multi-speaker meetings.

We'll upload the 24-hour sample logs to the Drive link you shared (RTP + token timestamps) by tomorrow EOD. Also, our SRE flagged first-token latency for H100-based inference images depending on cold-starts; happy to capture cold/warm-start split if that helps the matrix.

Ben / Marcus —

Forwarding the Cerebro notes and the logs they promised (they dropped the file into our shared drive). Please prioritize a short hardware + ops comparison focused on low first-token latency and steady sustained throughput. Key constraints to cover in the matrix: 

- Tail latency (95/99) for streaming decode (first token and rolling tokens).
- Cost per sustained token (reserved pool amortized) and cost per burst-minute above reservation.
- Memory footprint for KV cache per concurrent stream and how many streams per GPU instance we can safely host.
- Quantization options and expected quality delta for L4/multi-L4 approach (would reduce cost but may increase token latency).

Keep recommendations simple: preferred stack for pilot (HW + model variant + reserved tokens/sec), recommended reserved pool size (in tokens/sec and in #GPUs), and a short fallback policy we can propose. Ben — you own the doc. Marcus — can you add a 3-step canary checklist once Ben posts recommendations?

Thanks — Hannah

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: Pilot readiness & ops check — dedicated hardware and streaming needs

Hannah / Marcus —

Attached is the HW comparison snapshot (rows are A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and multi-L4 cluster). High-level summary first: 

- Recommendation: Pilot on H100-80GB cluster for best tail latency and lower batch-sensitivity; reserve capacity for the steady 6k tokens/sec and allow a burst pool that covers +4k tokens/sec for 10-minute windows (cost model included).

- Latency: H100 median first-token RTT ~60–85ms warm, 140–200ms cold (depends on model and warmup). A100 warm first-token similar (70–95ms) but higher memory pressure for 60 concurrent streams at 800-token sequences. Multi-L4: best cost but first-token latency tends to be higher (120–220ms) and quality drop is measurable on longer contexts.

- Throughput / sizing: we estimate one H100 can sustain ~1,600 tokens/sec for streaming workloads with KV caching for 20 concurrent RT streams (avg seq 120). For 6k sustained: reserve 4 H100s (amortized safety factor x1.2). For burst headroom to 10k: add elastic burst pool of 2 extra H100s or configure burst routing to a multi-L4 fleet for cost-effective overflow.

- KV cache footprint: ~1.2GB per concurrent 800-token stream on H100 with current model. This is the driver behind needing fewer concurrent streams per GPU for long transcripts.

- Quantization: 4-bit quantization on L4 reduces memory and cost but increases generation latency slightly and degrades long-context coherence in our QA checks. Not recommended for initial pilot where transcript fidelity matters.

Deliverables attached: pilot_hardware_matrix.csv, cost-compare-estimates.xlsx, brief-canary-plan.txt.

Next steps I propose: 
1) We send this recommendation to Cerebro with the recommended reserved pool: 4 x H100 (reserved) + 2 x H100 (burst) OR reserved 4 H100 + overflow to multi-L4 for bursts (ops preference, cost tradeoff).
2) Marcus to add the canary checklist and rollback triggers.
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up with Cerebro to walk through the sizing and confirm the reserved vs overflow decision (I can do a cost sensitivity run live).

I'll upload the full matrix to the Drive link and flag the cells I want you both to review.
